chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abu al-Subbah, from Jabir, who said:

I heard a man saying to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have two parents who are non-Muslims (or adversaries).' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Be righteous to both of them, just as you are righteous to the Muslims who are not among those who love us.'

key_terms.بَرَّهُمَا: Be righteous to both of them
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّانَا: They love us / Are our allies

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim treat their non-Muslim parents according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that filial piety (*birr*) toward non-Muslim parents is obligatory and should mirror the kindness shown to Muslim relatives who are part of the Shia community (*mawalli*). This ruling emphasizes that the bond of kinship supersedes religious affiliation in matters of general courtesy and care, provided the parents do not force the child to commit shirk. The comparison to *mawalli* highlights the deep affection and loyalty Shias are expected to show to their co-religionists, setting a benchmark for the quality of care given to parents.
